sources.title: UK PRTR data sets guidance
facts: Updated 30 June 2026.
UK PRTR data includes facilities, locations, activities, releases to air/water/soil and off-site transfers.
Operator data may be measured, calculated, estimated or unspecified and is regulator quality-checked.

sources.title: Pollution Inventory general guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Requires annual mass releases and transfers and distinguishes point, fugitive and notifiable releases.
Below-reporting-threshold does not mean zero; measured, calculated and estimation techniques have distinct semantics.

sources.title: Pollution Inventory reporting collection
facts: Environment Agency collection for annual releases and transfers from regulated industrial activities.
Reporting workflow and collection membership are not emissions measurements.

sources.title: Pollution Inventory National Data Library
facts: Environment Agency dataset last updated 17 April 2026.
Provides downloadable Pollution Inventory files for reporting years through 2024.
Inventory boundary covers the permit/authorisation including point and fugitive sources, not cadastral parcels.

sources.title: UK PRTR industrial emissions data download
facts: Published 30 June 2026.
Provides annual UK PRTR datasets including the 2024 reporting-year XML.
Dataset rows require method, pollutant, medium, facility and reporting-year interpretation.

sources.title: PIEDC reporting system guidance
facts: Updated 20 December 2023.
Explains submission of Pollution Inventory and UK PRTR returns through PIEDC.
Submission workflow is not physical observation evidence.

sources.title: Pollution Inventory reporting codes
facts: Defines NOSE-P, NACE, PRTR, method and waste codes used in reporting.
Classification codes identify activity or methodology and do not quantify emissions by themselves.

sources.title: Pollution Inventory technical guidance and equations
facts: Provides equations and examples for release estimation.
Sampling concentration needs compatible flow and operating time to derive annual mass.
Calculated release remains distinct from direct measurement.

sources.title: Pollution Inventory reporting forms
facts: Official Environment Agency reporting forms for emissions, releases and transfers.
A completed form or deadline is reporting evidence, not independent physical measurement.

sources.title: Waste transfer station Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Guidance covers annual releases to air/water and waste movement for regulated transfer stations.
Waste throughput or transfer is not equivalent to greenhouse-gas release.

sources.title: Landfill Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Separates fugitive landfill-gas releases from point-source combustion in engines or flares.
Collected, combusted and fugitive gas must not be conflated.

sources.title: Intensive farming Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Sector guidance includes releases and transfers plus emission factors.
Emission factors require compatible activity data and do not create parcel observations.

sources.title: Mining and quarrying Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Defines reporting scope for underground mines and qualifying opencast mines/quarries.
Reporting eligibility or site area is not an emission measurement.

sources.title: Refineries Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Sector guidance identifies refinery pollutant sources including carbon dioxide from furnaces, boilers and turbines.
Source identification is distinct from annual quantified mass and parcel attribution.

sources.title: Cement lime and minerals Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Preferred release-estimation hierarchy starts with CEMS, then periodic monitoring, mass balance/emission factors and agreed alternatives.
Biomass and fossil carbon accounting boundaries must be preserved.

sources.title: Chemical treatment of waste Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Guidance includes fugitive emissions from delivery, storage and transfer operations.
Process presence or waste movement does not prove annual GHG mass.

sources.title: Ferrous and non-ferrous metals Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Official sector-specific Pollution Inventory guidance.
Release-estimation techniques and pollutant lists must be interpreted within facility and reporting-year scope.

sources.title: Incineration Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Prefers CEMS with flow integration, then periodic monitoring, mass balance or emission factors.
Waste feedstock or emission factors are not direct atmospheric measurements.

sources.title: Combustion Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Sector guidance covers emissions to air/water and off-site waste transfers.
Combustion activity and permit scope must not be promoted to parcel GHG without compatible observed mass and geometry.

sources.title: Food and drink Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Identifies CO2 and methane sources including fermentation and biogas flaring/venting where applicable.
Process source lists are not annual parcel emissions.

sources.title: Paper and pulp Pollution Inventory guidance
facts: Updated 29 November 2024.
Sector guidance covers emissions to air/water and off-site transfers.
Facility-sector reporting does not establish cadastral parcel binding.

sources.title: Operator monitoring assessment guidance
facts: Environment Agency OMA assesses quality and reliability of permit-holder monitoring.
Assessment quality evidence is not itself an emission quantity.

sources.title: MCERTS monitoring collection
facts: Updated 27 April 2026.
Collection covers monitoring standards for stack, water, soil, ambient and other regulated measurements.
Certification/standards evidence must be separated from measurement results.

sources.title: Periodic stack monitoring techniques and standards
facts: Updated 2 July 2026.
Environment Agency index for choosing periodic stack monitoring techniques and standards.
A method standard does not itself provide a measured result.

sources.title: Continuous stack monitoring and sampling standards
facts: Updated 13 January 2026.
Covers CEMS, DAHS, long-term samplers and PEMS standards.
Continuous-monitoring infrastructure must be distinguished from actual validated emission data.

sources.title: CEMS quality assurance guidance
facts: Updated 28 March 2025.
Covers EN 14181 QAL requirements, calibration, ongoing QA and annual surveillance tests.
Calibration/QA status is not the pollutant mass itself.

sources.title: Carbon capture stack monitoring guidance
facts: Published 28 March 2025.
Defines monitoring approach for solvent-based post-combustion carbon capture plants including CO2 and solvent-breakdown products.
Captured CO2 and residual stack emissions require separate accounting boundaries.

sources.title: MCERTS industrial stack monitoring equipment
facts: Updated 28 August 2024.
Covers certification of CEMS, transportable systems and other stack monitors.
Equipment certification is not a site emission result.

sources.title: Stack emissions measurement locations
facts: Guidance applies EN 15259 principles for representative stack sampling locations.
Representative sampling design affects measurement validity but is not an annual emission value.

sources.title: Low-risk MCP and specified-generator stack monitoring
facts: Current Environment Agency guidance for monitoring low-risk MCPs and specified generators.
Allows appropriate certified continuous or periodic monitoring for relevant pollutants.
ELV compliance monitoring must not be confused with GHG parcel measurement.

sources.title: MCERTS low-risk plant monitors
facts: Low-risk monitors can support indicative or specified regulatory monitoring.
The guidance explicitly says these monitors are not suitable for quantitative IED measurements.

sources.title: MCERTS handheld emissions monitoring systems
facts: Updated 16 January 2026.
HEMS can cover stack, landfill-borehole, methane, CO2, oxygen and flow measurements.
HEMS are not suitable for quantitative IED compliance measurement.

sources.title: MCERTS long-term samplers of carbon dioxide
facts: Updated 25 July 2025.
Standard covers samplers used to determine biogenic versus fossil-derived CO2 ratio.
Sampler certification does not include transport, laboratory analysis or reporting of results.

sources.title: MCERTS manual stack monitoring organisations
facts: Updated 17 July 2024.
Sets accreditation requirements for organisations performing manual stack monitoring.
Organisation accreditation is not an emissions observation.

sources.title: MCERTS manual stack monitoring examination syllabuses
facts: Updated 14 April 2025.
Defines personnel competency levels and technical endorsements for manual stack monitoring.
Personnel competence is supporting QA evidence, not emission quantity.

sources.title: Landfill gas engine emissions monitoring LFTGN08
facts: Environment Agency guidance for monitoring spark-ignition landfill-gas engine emissions.
Engine exhaust measurements must remain distinct from fugitive landfill methane and flare emissions.

sources.title: MCERTS self-monitoring of liquid flow
facts: Updated 28 August 2024.
Applies to permitted sewage or trade-effluent liquid-flow monitoring.
Liquid flow alone is not pollutant mass or greenhouse-gas emission.

sources.title: MCERTS event-duration monitor installation and use
facts: Updated 28 August 2024.
Covers event-duration monitors at wastewater overflows and related permitted locations.
Event duration is not discharge volume, pollutant mass or GHG emission.

sources.title: MCERTS ambient monitoring equipment
facts: Updated 9 September 2025.
Defines performance standards for ambient air monitoring systems and sensors.
Ambient concentration must not be promoted to stack or parcel annual mass without a valid model/boundary.

sources.title: MCERTS flow and EDM inspector competency
facts: Current Environment Agency competency standard for flow and EDM inspectors.
Inspector competency supports quality assurance and is not a physical emissions observation.
